text:
ashley: Noticed a surge of 429s from the Node quickstart during the onboarding lab. Users paging embeddings in parallel blow past tenant burst.
omar: can repro locally. sample uses Promise.all over cursors, so it fires 10+ requests at once.
kevin: code snippet?
ashley: ```js
// naive parallel paging
await Promise.all(tokens.map(t => client.embeddings.page({ cursor: t })))
```
omar: yep. plus the SDK retry is immediate (no jitter) so failed pages instantly retry and magnify the burst.
kevin: SDK parity note: Python exposes a public RateLimiter class; JS keeps the runtime limiter private. that prevents samples from sharing a bucket.
ashley: short-term fix: change sample to use p-limit(3) or a small in-repo limiter and add a troubleshooting blurb in quickstart. long-term: export a thin createRateLimiter API from JS SDK.
omar: also saw token refresh race: when token refreshes happen mid-flight, a bunch of requests get 401 and then re-fire simultaneously. singleflight refresh would stop the thundering herd.
kevin: implement `auth.onceRefresh()` that returns the inflight refresh promise if present. tiny change, big win.
support-bot: created KB article draft: "Handling 429s when paginating embeddings". link (internal): https://kb.redwood-inference.dev/pagination-429s
ashley: add a small example for exponential backoff + jitter for retries: `delay = Math.min(2000, 100 * 2**attempt) * (0.7 + Math.random()*0.6)`. keeps retries spread out.
omar: also propose adding `concurrency` option to paginator helper: `for await (const p of client.embeddings.paginate(q, { concurrency: 2 })) {}` — ergonomic and prevents changing user code flow.
kevin: I'll prep two PRs: (1) sample change + KB update (today), (2) export rateLimiter + paginator concurrency + auth.onceRefresh (next week).
deploy-bot: preview site with sample patch: https://deployments.redwood-inference.dev/pr/611
support-bot: added short support checklist: "If you see 429s: 1) reduce concurrency, 2) use SDK rate limiter or p-limit, 3) ensure auth singleflight, 4) enable jittered backoff"
ashley: also adding `x-client-concurrency` header in sample client calls so support can correlate high-concurrency clients in logs. low risk, high signal.
omar: agreed. ok let's ship the quick patch now.
